displayOrder.name: Expandable Projects
displayOrder.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Create a realistic, production-quality PokeTaskBar macOS desktop PROJECTS page continuing the attached approved designs. Image 1 is the approved Issues page, especially its project grouping, compact rows and optional right panels. Image 2 is the approved Today shell. Carry their precise typography, controls and native window language into the new page.
Target 1488 x 1056, same landscape viewport as references. Current date Friday 18 September 2026. One straight-on app screenshot with readable type, complete native window, generous purposeful whitespace. No concept title, number, annotations, surrounding marketing or browser frame.
Preserve expanded left navigation approximately 240px: PokeTaskBar identity, Cody, Search, Today, Focus, Issues, Projects, Initiatives, Collection, Usage, Settings bottom. Projects selected. Native traffic lights, back/forward controls, compact Projects page tab and sidebar-collapse controls. Both sidebars resizable/collapsible.
Visual invariants: continuous #EFF0F2 outer shell; inset #F8F8FA main content canvas with rounded corners and open gutters on every edge including bottom. White supporting panels only where useful. Ink #242528, metadata #73757B, restrained semantic accents, quiet neutral selection fill, dark primary button. Readable SF Pro-like type, 14-16pt rows, restrained 28-32pt page heading, small consistent outline icons. NO permanent sidebar separator strokes, edge-to-edge section rules or resize grip dots; hover-only boundary guides are invisible in this resting state. Do not create card outlines for every label or row. Use spacing, alignment and surface tones.
Primary workflow: browse a project, read its purpose, review its issues, then choose an issue to focus on. Preserve existing In progress / Production project tabs, project name, status, lead, target date, description, nested issues and Open in Linear. Support modest Find a project search and refresh/sync feedback. Do not invent project creation, kanban boards, Gantt charts, health scores, budgets, sprints, activity feeds or percentage-complete metrics. A New issue button can appear in selected project context, but no New project button.
Illustrative project data: four In progress projects: PokeTaskBar (4 issues, lead Cody, target 30 Sep 2026), Markdown Notes (3 issues, target 5 Oct 2026), Focus Assistant (2 issues, target 9 Oct 2026), Capture Workflow (2 issues, target 12 Oct 2026). All lead Cody. Selected project is PokeTaskBar. Description 'A calm companion for focused work, connected to Linear.' Its issues: SPA-142 Refine PokeTaskBar navigation; SPA-148 Polish menu-bar controls; SPA-151 Check sidebar resizing; SPA-139 Review focus session notes. Status In progress. Tiny quiet sync text Synced just now. Project dates are future targets anchored to 18 Sep 2026. Show 4 In progress projects; Production can be an unselected tab without a count.
No giant Pokémon or timer on this page. Keep primary project/issue navigation in the main canvas, usable when optional right extras are hidden. Focus can start from a selected issue only, never from an entire project. All secondary content supports reaching that task. Use exact short copy and clean natural spacing with no clipped content.

Direction: Expandable Projects.
This is the closest continuation of the approved Issues list: wide main canvas and an expanded approximately 300px right extras rail. Header Projects with In progress 4 and Production tabs, Find a project search, understated refresh. Display four projects as unboxed grouped rows with small disclosure arrows, project icon, strong project name and muted metadata aligned at the trailing edge.
PokeTaskBar is expanded first: header shows 4 issues and target 30 Sep. Four indented compact issue rows beneath use status glyphs, IDs and titles. Highlight the first issue SPA-142 with a soft neutral fill, with a small dark Start focus button at the trailing edge and 25 min beside it. Other projects are collapsed rows below: Markdown Notes, Focus Assistant, Capture Workflow, each with issue count, lead Cody and target date. No permanent horizontal rules; spacing expresses the project groups.
The right rail uses two separate white rounded panels. Top 'Project details' with Status In progress, Lead Cody, Target date 30 Sep 2026. Bottom 'About this project' with the short PokeTaskBar description and a small Open in Linear action. Only subtle local control outlines, no separator lines. All four projects and the expanded issues fit comfortably above the bottom gutter. Prioritise a clean scanning experience and an immediate path into focus.
